titulo: Phone calls, invitations and arranging to meet: Inviting, accepting and declining

aula.titulo: Phone calls, invitations and arranging to meet
aula.objetivo: Answer and make a phone call («¿Diga?», «Soy…», «¿Está…?»), leave a message, invite with «apetecer» and «¿quieres…?», accept and decline politely, and arrange a time and place with «quedar» and «nos vemos».

itens.pt: Do you feel like…? Do you fancy…?
Do you want to come to…?
OK. / All right. («Vale» is typical of Spain)

blocos.titulo: Inviting with apetecer, quieres and qué tal si
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: in Spain, the most common verb for inviting is «apetecer», which works like «gustar»: the thing you feel like is the subject, and the person goes in «te / os / le». «¿Te apetece ir al cine?» (Do you feel like going to the cinema?), «¿Te apetece un café?» (Do you fancy a coffee?). For several people: «¿Os apetece cenar con nosotros?». After «apetecer» comes an infinitive or a noun — English "feel like GOING" becomes the infinitive «ir», never a gerund. STEP 2: other ways, used all over the Spanish-speaking world: «¿Quieres venir a cenar el sábado?», «¿Por qué no vamos al cine?» (Why don't we…?), «¿Qué tal si quedamos el viernes?» (How about meeting on Friday?) and, more politely, «¿Te gustaría venir?». STEP 3: to accept: «Sí, claro», «Vale» (Spain), «De acuerdo», «Me encantaría» (I'd love to), «Con mucho gusto». In Latin America, «de acuerdo» and «bueno» are more common. STEP 4: to decline politely, use three parts: thank, give the reason, suggest another day. «Gracias, pero hoy no puedo. Tengo que trabajar. ¿Lo dejamos para otro día?» or «Me encantaría, pero ya tengo un plan». A bare «No quiero» sounds as rude as "I don't want to". STEP 5: to talk about a plan, use «ir a» + infinitive (lesson 30): «Voy a visitar a mi abuela», «Vamos a cenar con unos amigos». STEP 6: «invitar» has two meanings: to invite and to treat (pay). «Te invito al cine» can mean "I'm inviting you to the cinema" and also "the cinema's on me". «Invito yo» means "it's on me" / "my treat". Note English "invite TO" = «invitar A» (a + el = al). STEP 7: give the reason with «tener que» (lesson 13): «Tengo que estudiar», «Tengo que cuidar de mi hermano». STEP 8: to check a time works: «¿Te va bien?», «¿Te viene bien?» (Does that suit you?).
blocos.comparacao: English "Do you feel like going…?" becomes «¿Te apetece ir…?» — «apetecer» works like «gustar» and takes the infinitive, not «-ando/-iendo». English "invite TO" is «invitar A», and «invitar» also means "to pay for someone": «Invito yo» = "It's on me".

tabela.traducao: Do you feel like going to the cinema?
Do you want to come for dinner on Saturday?
Would you like to come to my place?

tabela.frase: Gracias, pero hoy no puedo. Tengo que trabajar.
tabela.traducao: Thanks, but I can't today. I have to work.
Shall we leave it for another day?

erros.motivo: English "invite TO" is «invitar a» (a + el = al), not «para».

erros.certo: Gracias, pero hoy no puedo. ¿Lo dejamos para otro día?
erros.motivo: A blunt refusal sounds cold; thank, explain and suggest another day.
After «encantar» comes the infinitive, with no «de».

blocos.enunciado: Invite three different people out loud: a friend (tú), a colleague (usted) and two friends (vosotros, with «os apetece»). Then accept one invitation and politely decline another.
Say out loud how you would answer the phone, say who you are and ask to speak to someone.
